challenge.better_approach: Passing the venv bin on PATH into systemd-run only moves the dependency; the Windows path already settled on the caller's interpreter.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That sys.executable in the caller is always a python that has the bus's imports. It is, for every caller that already imported remote.py from the repo.
challenge.prior_art: 0156856b1fae / background_python (windowless_spawn.py:32) measured the same psycopg2 death on Windows 2026-11-12. 404f193284ac is the install-time check, a different seam.
challenge.real_collision: None; it extends background_python's settled why to Linux.

answers.falsifier: Under PATH=/usr/bin:/bin a scratch bus spawned through both paths comes up and imports psycopg2; the argv tooth reds when 'python3' is restored. Wrong intent if a systemd unit must not run a venv interpreter.
answers.how: remote.py _spawn (:214) and _setsid (:276) take background_python() (sys.executable) in place of 'python3', as _detached (:262) already does. A proof captures the argv each path would run, with the subprocess calls stubbed, and asserts argv[0] is the caller's interpreter under a PATH that holds no python3.
answers.traces_to: Law 3 (measured: 29 'no bus' reds under a stripped PATH) and CP6 (safety built, not assumed from PATH).
answers.what: The Linux bus spawn runs the caller's own interpreter, so a bus never dies because PATH found a different python3.

bullets.text: a bus spawn failure shows only in bus.log; the caller sees FileNotFoundError on bus.sock

title: The Linux bus spawn runs the caller's own interpreter, so a bus never dies because PATH found a different python3.
